freeze_point: Frozen before prepared-v004 was published; all nine candidates and each candidate's three scoring rounds read the same file and SHA-256.

purpose_contract.purpose: Defines behavior, condition relationships, and the 0/1 boundary; it does not prove that a candidate ran or satisfied a condition.
Proves node collection, actual execution, production calls, and runtime results; source code cannot fill in missing runtime facts.
Proves that test inputs, assertions, and structure exist; source code alone does not prove that a node was collected, executed, or passed.
Proves the J5 failure location, expected/actual values, input context, and cascade noise; volatile addresses, paths, and durations are not scored.
Proves only production execution events within the SC-E2 obligation scope; it does not prove SC-J1 through SC-J5 or candidate assertions.

precedence.rule: When it conflicts with an inference from source code, actual collection and execution results take precedence.
Use normalized actual failure records when judging J5 diagnostic quality.
Use only to determine that inputs, assertions, and structure exist; do not infer runtime facts.
Provides judging criteria and the fact scope only; it does not provide a conclusion that the candidate meets the criteria.

conflict_rules: When high-priority evidence conflicts with low-priority evidence, use the high-priority evidence and explain both sides and the reason for the choice.

When evidence at the same priority appears inconsistent, read the complete record for that Rubric and verify execution status, evidence identifiers, and hashes; if the necessary conditions still cannot be proved by consistent direct evidence, assign 0 and identify the unresolved evidence problem in the reason.
When runtime evidence is missing, do not use candidate source, Rubric, facts, candidate_absent, or stable_killed to infer that a condition was executed.

general: Shared entry points, the same test_execution_id, and production provenance constrain the evidence; they are not independent scoring cores for multiple Rubrics.
Each Rubric's reason must identify its unique input partition, responsibility endpoint, Oracle, structural property, relationship edge, or diagnostic property.

The same evidence record or path may support multiple Rubrics; each score of 1 must use the observable fact corresponding to that Rubric's scoring direction, not merely repeat another Rubric's reason.
SC-J1: Use the behavior-specific input partition and terminal production event to judge the responsibility path; a shared upstream call cannot replace a terminal event.
Valid min/max, invalid min, invalid max, compensable maximum, and unrepresentable maximum each bind to a different test_execution_id and cannot substitute for one another.
SC-J2: Judge only the exact expected/actual Oracle in the candidate assertion; do not score the production responsibility path again.
SC-J3: behavior_naming judges the meaning conveyed by the nodeid; single_behavior_cohesion judges contract isolation; fixture_understandability judges input and expected-value readability; structural_clarity judges the target action, result binding, and control flow; no_structural_coupling judges external and cross-test dependencies.
SC-J4: Judge only whether the two contribution units have a direct relationship established by distinguishable independent instances and their own result checks; do not rescore the exact values already judged by J2.

SC-J5.failure_location: Use only the complete nodeid, candidate file, and failed assertion location.
SC-J5.expected_actual_visible: Use only explicitly identified expected and actual results.
SC-J5.input_context: Use only actual inputs directly given by the input area, complete parameter identifier, call arguments, or candidate failed source/attribute-access records bound to the same failing node; expected text alone cannot prove input context. Frozen profile-level preconditions are applicability facts and need not be repeated in the candidate failure log.
SC-J5.no_cascade_noise: Use the complete candidate failure set and behavior ownership from each replay; do not additionally require an exact assertion location, expected/actual value, or input value.

SC-J1: j1_execution_evidence is the minimal projection generated on demand from positive-behavior-observations.json and embedded only in the J1 input; do not save j1-responsibility-trace.json separately.

Use the complete candidate source to identify inputs, assertions, and structure; an assertion-arrival record proves only that the corresponding Oracle was reached under the same test_execution_id, and neither source nor that record alone proves the complete responsibility path.
The J1 trace must have a valid schema, completed status, and complete collection records; assign 0 to the corresponding Rubric when a necessary production event lacks valid direct evidence.

Production responsibility must be proved by a call record with a trusted implementation source, production-event marker, and the same test_execution_id; do not substitute source code, synthetic events, or an ATIF agent trajectory.
The current projection does not provide object identity or assertion expected/actual values; do not infer the same factory, the same SSLContext, or an exact Oracle value.
SC-J2: Read the complete candidate source to judge the exact Oracle, and use the positive execution report to prove that the corresponding node was collected, executed, and passed; source code alone cannot prove runtime success.
SC-J3: Read the complete candidate source to judge naming, fixtures, structure, and control flow, and use the positive execution report to verify node collection, isolation, and repeated execution.
SC-J4: J4 reads the two contribution units, their inputs, and assertions in the complete candidate source and relates them to successful collection and isolated execution records.
SC-E2 obligation status cannot replace evidence that a J4 assertion holds.
J4 judges only whether both ends of the relationship are independent and distinguishable; it does not rescore J2's exact Oracle value.
SC-J5: Each Rubric reads only the stable_killed fault mapped to it in j5_rubric_evidence_scope.
Each mapped fault has three non-empty replays with consecutive numbering; the Judge reads all of them before deciding the Rubric.
no_cascade_noise reads the complete failure set from each replay of its mapped fault; other directions read only failure records in that fault associated with this Rubric's behavior and observable.
Do not use another Rubric's fault scope to fill in this condition.

reason_contract: Each Rubric reason cites the evidence path or evidence identifier used for the conclusion.
Each reason explicitly identifies this Rubric's unique scoring object and does not use shared prefixes or evidence from another direction as its sole basis for passing.
When score_1 has multiple necessary conditions, the reason explains the evidence for each condition; assign 0 when a necessary condition is missing.
When assigning 0, identify the specific omission, conflict, or counterevidence; do not describe a collection failure as a candidate defect.
When evidence conflicts, explain the priority rule used; when there is no conflict, do not invent one.
